items.title: Arrests made in GTA firearm trafficking network linked to 14 shootings in region: Peel police
items.summary: Peel police say they have arrested four people in connection with an alleged firearm trafficking network, which investigators say was linked to 14 different shootings in the Greater Toronto Area.

items.title: Whistleblower hotline will let Mississauga residents report wrongdoing at the city
items.summary: Starting in early 2027, Mississauga residents will be able to confidentially report concerns related to alleged fraud, waste or wrongdoing at the city under the municipality’s expanded Whistleblower Program. The City of Mississauga’s new fraud and waste hotline, set to launch sometime in the first three months of next year, will provide both city employees and the public with “an independent and confidential reporting mechanism that strengthens accountability and reinforces public trust in the integrity of city operations,” a staff report to be discussed at general committee on Wednesday reads. The city established its Whistleblower Program in 2014 to provide employees with an independent and confidential mechanism to anonymously report workplace wrongdoing, the report from Amy Truong, the city’s internal audit director, noted. “Over the past decade, the program has supported accountability, ethical conduct and a workplace culture where concerns can be raised without fear of reprisal,” Truong’s report continued. ” The enhancements “are intended to strengthen transparency and public confidence in the city’s governance and oversight framework,” the report further stated. Once up and running, the new hotline will provide city workers and the public with a confidential way in which to report concerns related to fraud, waste or wrongdoing “that may affect the integrity, accountability and effective stewardship of city operations,” Truong wrote in the report. City councillors and staff also discussed back in March the idea of hiring an auditor general to ensure accountability to the public.

items.title: Gun call leads to 4 arrests and $65K in seized drugs in Mississauga
items.summary: A report of a man sitting in a car with a gun in the heart of Mississauga has led police to four arrests and the recovery of an estimated $65,000 in drugs. Peel Regional Police said the initial call was received just over two weeks ago, on Sept. 7, when it was reported that a man in a vehicle was armed with a gun in the area of Hurontario and Dundas streets in the Cooksville neighbourhood. Once on the scene, police officers quickly located a man who was found to be in possession of an illegal firearm and a separate magazine containing ammunition, police said. The responding officers also located and seized “a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl with an estimated value of $65,000,” Peel police said on Tuesday. A man was subsequently arrested by officers with the Peel police 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau. Following further investigation and the execution of a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, three additional people were arrested, according to police.

items.title: Four people arrested, $65K worth of drugs seized in Mississauga
items.summary: Four people have been arrested after police seize tens of thousands of dollars worth of suspected cocaine and fentanyl as well as an illegal firearm in Mississauga earlier this month. According to Peel Regional Police, on Sept. 7, police were called to the area of Hurontario Street and Dundas Street West after receiving reports of a man who was armed while inside a vehicle. Officers located the first suspect, who was found to be in possession of an illegal firearm as well as a “separate magazine with multiple rounds of ammunition,” police said in a news release. Officers said they also located a quantity of substances believed to be cocaine and fentanyl, worth an estimated $65,000. During an investigation, police say they then executed a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, where three additional suspects were arrested. Olamilekan Jimoh, 26, of Mississauga, was charged with multiple offences, including careless storage of a firearm, weapon, prohibited device or ammunition; failure to comply with an undertaking; and possession of a firearm with attempts to conceal. Jimoh was also charged with four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Modupe Abijo, 52, and Omobodunrin Jimoh, 28, of Mississauga, were charged with four counts each of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Cleo Romi Reynods, 45, of Toronto, was charged with failure to comply with a release order.

items.title: Mississauga’s staff-only whistleblower program is being reshaped into a public hotline residents may use by 2027
items.summary: After the unanimous vote, councillors stood for a moment of … Drivers — not homeowners — would face the fine under the pro… Residents will be able to anonymously report financial misuse and wrongdoing at city hall — a program previously open only to staff since 2014. A staff report outlines the plan for the city’s Fraud and Waste Hotline, expected to launch in early 2027 for the public. By early 2027, Mississauga residents could begin reporting municipal fraud and financial waste through the city’s Fraud and Waste Hotline. A report is coming to general committee on Sept. 23 which outlines an implementation plan on how the city’s existing internal whistleblower program will be made public and renamed as the Fraud and Waste Hotline. The move follows a staff report in March, which came in response to resident demands for better financial oversight. In the report, staff provided four recommendations and council opted to expand the internal audit division.

items.title: Vehicle Owners, Not Homeowners, Would Take the Hit Under Mississauga's Proposed Lawn-Parking Fines
items.summary: According to a staff report going to Mississauga's general committee on September 23, the city is considering a standalone bylaw that would fine vehicle owners, not property owners, for parking on residential lawns and other landscaped areas. The report recommends banning parking, standing and stopping on grass, gardens and other soft landscaped surfaces on residential properties, with fines set at $150 for standard vehicles and $375 for heavy or recreational vehicles. Violations would be handled through the city's Administrative Penalty System, letting municipal enforcement officers issue a penalty notice directly to a vehicle's registered owner regardless of who was actually driving. Under that system, according to the report, registered owners could dispute a penalty through the city's dispute resolution process. Staff say the change is meant to replace the current approach, which handles lawn parking complaints through the zoning bylaw, a process the report describes as time-consuming and resource-intensive because it requires investigating property conditions rather than simply the act of parking, along with mandatory warning periods, reinspections and potential court proceedings.

items.title: Packed Council Chambers Push Back on a Three-Tower Proposal Near the Etobicoke Border
items.summary: According to a report submitted to the City of Mississauga, residents packed council chambers to oppose an intensification proposal for a property at 4100 Ponytrail Drive and 1850 Rathburn Road East, in the northeast part of the city near the Etobicoke border. The property owner, Chelsea on the Green I Limited Partnership, submitted the proposal to the city in June, seeking to add three 20-storey apartment buildings totalling 695 units to the site. Two existing 18-storey apartment buildings on the property would remain, and the report notes a 25-storey building had previously been approved for the site by the Committee of Adjustment. The proposal requires an Official Plan amendment before it can proceed. Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca raised the development with residents in August as opposition to the plan began building ahead of the council discussion.

items.title: Peel Police Say a Mississauga House Was the Hub of a Multimillion-Dollar Dark Web Drug Ring
items.summary: Police say four people from across the Greater Toronto Area are facing numerous charges after investigators say they dismantled a multimillion-dollar dark web drug trafficking operation allegedly run out of a Mississauga home. According to police, the dark web is a concealed portion of the internet not indexed by conventional search engines and typically accessed only through specialized browsers, which investigators say made tracking the operation more difficult. As the investigation progressed, police say they identified members of the alleged distribution network and zeroed in on several addresses connected to it. Officers executed multiple search warrants on February 20, 2026, including at a residence in Mississauga that police allege was being used in the day-to-day operation of the online drug distribution network. Police say the investigation also recovered a quantity of drugs tied to the network's operations.

items.title: Gun Seized in Cross-Border Trafficking Bust Ties Back to a 2024 Mississauga Killing
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an undercover operation called Project Red Zone, run by the force's Specialized Enforcement Bureau alongside the US Department of Homeland Security and Criminal Intelligence Service Ontario, infiltrated and disrupted a firearms trafficking network operating across the Greater Toronto Area. According to police, the operation seized 23 firearms, 75 grams of cocaine, and more than 950 rounds of ammunition, along with several weapons that are prohibited in Canada. Investigators say one of the recovered firearms has been linked to a March 2024 homicide in Mississauga in which one man was killed and another seriously injured. Police say forensic analysis also tied the seized firearms to 14 separate shootings across the GTA. The investigation determined that 15 of the 23 firearms had originated in the United States before making their way into the trafficking network.

items.title: Washroom Upgrades This Fall Are Just a Preview of a Bigger Celebration Square Overhaul
items.summary: According to INsauga, construction is set to begin this fall at Celebration Square in downtown Mississauga following the venue's seasonal shutdown, though it is only a smaller step ahead of the much larger renovation planned for the outdoor space. The washrooms at the square will be temporarily closed during the work and are expected to reopen in mid-November. The bigger renovation, covering the nearly five-acre public gathering space, could see construction begin toward the end of 2027, the city has said. Plans for that larger project have grown since 2025, when the city first floated more modest improvements for early 2026, into a significantly bigger renewal that will reshape the venue over the next couple of years. Earlier proposals called for bigger, higher-resolution viewing screens and new artificial turf, with that turf-replacement work expected to close the lawn and surrounding pavement to the public for four to six weeks once it begins.
